answer.text: Gives investor the right to sell back to issuer at specified price
Is the same as a convertible

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 59 says a put provision gives bondholders the right to sell the bond back to the issuer at a predetermined price on specified dates; page 69 supports the holder-right framing. The Trap: Convertibles are equity-linked; putables still carry coupons and may be collateralised. Note: Source-backed by NISM-XXI-A pages 59 and 69.
